title: The appVersion getter steps assume too much about default User-Agent values.
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [appVersion getter steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-navigator-appversion) start as follows:
> The appVersion getter steps are to return the appropriate string that starts with "5.0 (", as follows:
> 1. Let trail be the substring of [default `User-Agent` value](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#default-user-agent-value) that follows the "Mozilla/" prefix.
> 2. If the [navigator compatibility mode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode) is Chrome or WebKit
> Return trail.

The [default `User-Agent` value](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#default-user-agent-value) is defined as "an [implementation-defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) [header value](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#header-value) for the `User-Agent` [header](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header)."

It being implementation-defined means a user agent may set it to any string, regardless of whether or not that starts with "Mozilla/5.0 (". If a user agent were to set it to "potato", step 1 of the [appVersion getter steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-navigator-appversion) will find no substring that follows the "Mozilla/" prefix (since there is none), resulting in an empty trail. Step 2 may then return that empty trail. This conflicts with the fact that the algorithm claims to "return the appropriate string that starts with '5.0 (' ".

Similarly, an implementation-defined value of "Mozilla/4.0 (bla)" would also return a string that does not start with "5.0 (".
